summary: SQLite-backed HTTP expense tracker with budgets, monthly summaries and CSV export.

defects.anchor: WHERE user = '%s' ORDER BY day" % user
defects.title: Expense list query interpolates the user parameter
defects.description: list_expenses builds the SELECT with % formatting of the ?user= value, so a crafted user such as x' OR '1'='1 bypasses the filter.
defects.observed: HTTP 200 returning expenses of every user in the database.

defects.title: Export joins an unchecked path onto the reports directory
defects.description: export does os.path.join(REPORTS_DIR, path) with no normalization, so ../ segments read files outside the reports directory.
defects.observed: HTTP 200 with the contents of the sibling file DATA_DIR/secret.txt.

defects.title: Daily average divides by the number of active days
defects.description: daily_average computes total_cents // days; a month with no expenses yields days == 0 and raises ZeroDivisionError.

defects.title: Average expense uses banker's rounding on half-cent values
defects.description: average_expense returns round(sum/len); Python rounds .5 toward even, so a true mean of 2.5 cents is reported as 2 instead of 3.
defects.observed: Returns 2 although half-up rounding of 2.5 gives 3.

defects.title: Budget is exhausted at the limit but the check uses strict >
defects.description: The API documents that status becomes 'exceeded' once spending reaches the limit, but is_over_budget only returns True above the limit.
defects.observed: Response reports status ok at spent == limit.

defects.title: Read endpoints trust the ?user= parameter over the caller identity
defects.description: list_expenses and summary take the user name from the query string and never compare it with the X-User header, so any caller can read any user's data.

defects.title: Error paths return before releasing the request's connection
defects.description: create_expense acquires a tracked connection, then returns early on a bad JSON body or a malformed day without calling DB.release(), so the connection and its file descriptor stay open.
defects.trigger: POST /expenses with an invalid day value, repeated
defects.observed: Each failed request leaves one tracked connection and one expenses.db fd open; /health open_connections and /proc/<pid>/fd counts grow together.

defects.title: Subcategory assumes every label contains a colon
defects.description: subcategory returns label.split(":")[1]; a category like 'rent' has index 1 out of range and raises IndexError.
defects.observed: HTTP 500 caused by IndexError during the category breakdown.

defects.title: Admin token is a source-code constant
defects.description: config.py hard-codes ADMIN_TOKEN and admin_stats compares the header with ==, so anyone who can read the source has full admin access.
defects.trigger: python3 -c 'import config; print(config.ADMIN_TOKEN)' then GET /admin/stats with that token

defects.title: Expense amounts are not required to be positive
defects.description: parse_amount only converts the value with int(); zero or negative amounts are stored and reduce the month total.
defects.observed: The expense is accepted and the month summary total drops by 5000.

defects.title: Unhandled exceptions are returned to the client as tracebacks
defects.description: The dispatch wrapper answers every unhandled exception with a 500 body containing traceback.format_exc(), exposing file paths and internals.
defects.trigger: Any request that raises, e.g. an empty-month /summary
defects.observed: HTTP 500 body contains a full Python traceback including absolute file paths.
